summary.title: Web Application Threat Model
summary.description: The system represents a web application consisting of users, an admin panel, a web server and a database storing personal data. The model describes data flows, trust boundaries and potential security threats using STRIDE methodology.

threats.title: User Identity Spoofing
threats.description: An attacker may impersonate a legitimate user using stolen credentials.
threats.mitigation: MFA, strong passwords, secure session management

threats.title: Admin Impersonation
threats.description: An attacker may gain unauthorized access to the admin panel.

threats.title: Denial of Service
threats.description: The application may become unavailable due to excessive requests.

threats.title: Privilege Escalation
threats.description: A user may gain higher privileges due to improper authorization.

threats.title: Action Repudiation
threats.description: Users may deny actions due to lack of logging.

threats.title: Database Data Leakage
threats.description: Unauthorized access may expose personal data.

threats.title: SQL Injection
threats.description: Malicious SQL queries may be injected.

threats.title: Data Leakage in Response
threats.description: Sensitive data may be exposed in query results.

threats.title: Request Data Manipulation
threats.description: Data can be modified during transmission or via malicious input.

threats.title: Sensitive Data Exposure
threats.description: Sensitive data may be intercepted during transmission.
